classification.difficultyReason: Sketch each supplied y=kx² curve on shared axes using its common vertex, symmetry, coefficient sign and relative width, with simple substituted points. The positive coefficient in b(iii) requires an upward-opening curve. These are direct applications of taught transformations without an unsignposted connection.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch the graphs of these parabolas on the one set of axes.

answer.worked:
The vertex is $(0,0)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=0$.

$$\begin{align*}y(1)&=1^2\\y(1)&=1\end{align*}$$

Plot $(1,1)$ and $(-1,1)$ and draw the upward-opening parabola on the shared axes.

answer.short: Upward-opening parabola with vertex $(0,0)$, through $(\pm1,3)$; narrower than $y=x^2$.
answer.worked:
$y=3x^2$ is obtained by stretching $y=x^2$ by factor $3$ from the $x$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y(1)&=3(1)^2\\y(1)&=3\end{align*}$$

Plot $(0,0)$ and $(\pm1,3)$ and draw the narrower upward-opening parabola on the shared axes.

answer.short: Upward-opening parabola with vertex $(0,0)$, through $(\pm1,\frac13)$; wider than $y=x^2$.
answer.worked:
$y=\frac13x^2$ is obtained by scaling the ordinates of $y=x^2$ by $\frac13$.

$$\begin{align*}y(1)&=\frac13(1)^2\\y(1)&=\frac13\end{align*}$$

Plot $(0,0)$ and $(\pm1,\frac13)$ and draw the wider upward-opening parabola on the shared axes.

spec.description: Three equation-driven parabolas on one set of ungridded axes; dash patterns distinguish the curves.
spec.mathematics: y=x², y=3x² and y=x²/3 share vertex (0,0) and axis x=0.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Sketch the graphs of these parabolas on the one set of axes.

answer.worked:
Reflect $y=x^2$ in the $x$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y(1)&=-(1)^2\\y(1)&=-1\end{align*}$$

Plot $(0,0)$ and $(\pm1,-1)$ and draw the downward-opening parabola on the shared axes.

answer.short: Downward-opening parabola with vertex $(0,0)$, through $(\pm1,-3)$; narrower than $y=-x^2$.
answer.worked:
Stretch $y=x^2$ by factor $3$ from the $x$-axis, then reflect in the $x$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y(1)&=-3(1)^2\\y(1)&=-3\end{align*}$$

Plot $(0,0)$ and $(\pm1,-3)$ and draw the narrower downward-opening parabola on the shared axes.

The positive coefficient gives an upward-opening parabola. Scale the ordinates of $y=x^2$ by $\frac13$.

$$\begin{align*}y(1)&=\frac13(1)^2\\y(1)&=\frac13\end{align*}$$

Plot $(0,0)$ and $(\pm1,\frac13)$ and draw the upward-opening parabola on the shared axes.

spec.description: Two downward-opening curves and one upward-opening curve, following the printed student equations. The teacher's negative third coefficient is not adopted.
spec.mathematics: y=-x², y=-3x² and y=x²/3 share vertex (0,0) and axis x=0.

children.prompt: Sketch the graphs of these parabolas on the one set of axes.

answer.short: Upward-opening parabola with vertex $(0,0)$, through $(\pm1,1)$; widest of the three.
answer.worked:
The vertex is $(0,0)$ and the axis is $x=0$.

$$\begin{align*}y(1)&=1^2\\y(1)&=1\end{align*}$$

Plot $(0,0)$ and $(\pm1,1)$ and draw the widest of the three upward-opening curves on the shared axes.

answer.short: Upward-opening parabola with vertex $(0,0)$, through $(\pm1,2)$; between the other two in width.
answer.worked:
Stretch $y=x^2$ by factor $2$ from the $x$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}y(1)&=2(1)^2\\y(1)&=2\end{align*}$$

Plot $(0,0)$ and $(\pm1,2)$ and draw the curve between $y=x^2$ and $y=3x^2$ on the shared axes.

answer.short: Upward-opening parabola with vertex $(0,0)$, through $(\pm1,3)$; narrowest of the three.
answer.worked:

Plot $(0,0)$ and $(\pm1,3)$ and draw the narrowest upward-opening curve on the shared axes.
